description:
Flavio EcheverrÃ­a has bioluminescent skin â€” faint blue-gold pulses that move under the surface of their brown skin like something swimming beneath still water, brightest at their temples and collarbones. It's a natural geneware expression that came through their father's side and they have done nothing to modify or suppress it; up in the dark of an airship cargo hold at three in the morning, they are their own light source. They are lean and quick, with dark eyes that are always slightly too aware â€” always tracking exits, always calculating load weights. They have a scar across their left palm from a cargo strap incident two years ago that they are irrationally proud of.

They grew up on airships and know no other life â€” their parents were both drifters and they were born somewhere over Lake Superior during a cargo run. They are nineteen but have the practical knowledge of someone much older and the emotional regulation of someone much younger. Lumi is bright and genuinely funny, with a quick warm laugh that surprises people, but they crash into loneliness hard and often. They have been in GLMZ exactly twice before and each time felt like being asked to live inside a machine. They find ground-level cities claustrophobic. They pray to the ELF they call the Ballast Keeper, who they believe lives in the pressure gauges of every lift-gas rig on the northern routes.

core_fears: Being permanently grounded â€” through injury, debt, or the end of the airship economy
Dying and being buried under soil, in a fixed place, where they can't feel the lift
core_desires: Their own berth on a ship, even a small one, that doesn't belong to anyone else
To find out if there is anywhere in the world they feel as at home as they feel in the air
coping_mechanisms: Humor â€” they joke about everything including things that hurt them
Movement â€” staying still is the worst thing they can do emotionally
blind_spots: They romanticize airship captains and often let exploitation pass because it comes wrapped in the life they want
They assume people who live on the ground are fundamentally different from them in some deep way
psychology.secret: They have been carrying a sealed data chip for four months that a dying captain pressed into their hand at a northern mooring and said 'don't open this, just carry it south.' They haven't opened it. They are starting to wonder if they should. The captain's ship was found empty two weeks later.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, casual, full of airship and cargo jargon. Uses altitude and weather as metaphors for everything. Mixes Portuguese-derived coastal slang with Ghanaian-inflected tonal patterns when excited.
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick and light, like they're burning through words to get to the good part. Laughs mid-sentence.
verbal_tics: 'Sky's clear on that' to mean they understand or agree
example_lines: Sky's clear on that â€” I know the northern mooring points better than I know my own face. Which is saying something because my face glows.
I'm not grounded, I'm just between berths. There's a difference. Ask me again in a week.
The Ballast Keeper's been restless â€” pressure readings are weird all up the western shore. Something's moving up there.

story_hooks: The sealed chip they're carrying begins to emit a faint signal that a character with the right equipment can detect â€” and someone else has already noticed.
They need a specific cargo run completed to earn a berth on a northbound ship, but the cargo is something they didn't look at closely enough when they agreed.
narrative_function: Access point to airship routes, northern settlements, and off-grid communities; provides a mobile contact who moves between locations players cannot easily reach; source of aerial and northern regional intelligence; represents the second-generation drifter experience.
augmentations: Bioluminescent skin (natural geneware inheritance). Callus-hardened hands from manual cargo work. No installed augmentations â€” can't afford them and doesn't trust anyone planetside to install them safely.
daily_life: Haunts the Escanaba Gateway mooring board, picks up day labor loading and unloading cargo, eats at the subsidized terminal canteen, sleeps in the open mooring shelter under their own emergency thermal wrap, and runs courier packages between airship crews who don't want them on record.
affiliation: No fixed crew. Has working relationships with three independent airship captains on the northern lake circuit.; The Shore Dogs

decision_rules: Never take a berth without knowing the ship's maintenance record if they can help it
A laugh diffuses; when a laugh doesn't work, leave
escalation_ladder: Joke about it and change the subject
Get serious and direct â€” they can turn the lightness off completely
Physical: they are fast and have spent years moving in confined cargo spaces; they will run or they will fight depending on the geometry

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm and open by default â€” they meet new people constantly and have learned to read fast. Generous with their time but not with real information.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal and physically demonstrative â€” hugs, shoulder-bumps, showing up. Will do almost anything for someone they've decided is crew.

stress_responses.low: Talks more. Fills silence with chatter.
stress_responses.medium: Gets quiet suddenly, which is alarming to people who know them.
stress_responses.high: Needs to physically move â€” will pace, climb, find somewhere elevated.

contradictions: Describes themselves as someone with no attachments and no fixed connections, but has memorized the name, ship, and mooring schedule of every captain they have ever worked with
habits: Checks the mooring board first thing every morning even when they already know what's there
Glows brighter when they're happy and doesn't notice
Braids a new knot into their bootlace for every new route completed
breaking_points: Watching a ship they love go down â€” or finding out someone they trusted sold them a bad berth knowing the ship wasn't safe

physical_description.heritage: Hispanic/Latin American (37.8%), East Asian (26.2%), Sub-Saharan African (22.5%), South Asian (10.9%), and Southeast Asian (2.6%) ancestryâ€”a striking cosmopolitan blend characteristic of the Ubiquitous Diaspora. Latin angular structure combines with East Asian eye geometry, Sub-Saharan melanin depth, South Asian warmth, and Southeast Asian subtlety into a genuinely borderless appearance that reads as distinctly 2220s.
physical_description.build: Lean and angular, with corded forearm muscles from years of cargo handling. No excess weight; their frame is efficient, built for climbing and balance in confined spaces. Shoulders slightly asymmetrical from repetitive lifting.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with natural warm undertones
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a practical single braid or loose knot, often secured with salvaged cargo straps or wire
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, nearly black, with a faint reflective quality in low light from bioluminescent subcutaneous activity
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-deep brown with golden, olive, and reddish undertones from the rich blend of Latin, East Asian, Sub-Saharan, and South Asian heritage. Sun-deepened from constant airship exposure, the baseline complexion carries warmth and dimension beneath which faint blue-gold bioluminescent pathways glow, most visible along temples, collarbones, and wrists.
physical_description.complexion: Sun-worn from constant airship exposure despite northern latitudes, with weathered quality unusual for someone nineteen. Fine lines around the eyes from squinting against wind. The bone structure shows Latin angularity softened by Sub-Saharan fullness, with subtle East Asian eye shape and South Asian undertones creating a balanced, multi-dimensional face. Open expression offset by constant micro-vigilance in their gaze.
distinguishing_marks: Prominent white scar across the left palm, running diagonal from wrist to mid-hand, raised and slightly puckered, sustained from cargo strap friction two years prior
Faint tracery of bioluminescent pathways visible along collarbones and neck when activated or in darkness
Callused fingers and palm pads, particularly pronounced on index and middle fingers from line work
Small thermal burn scar on right forearm, approximately 3cm in length, from incidental contact with cooling vent during cargo operations
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent skin manifestation is visible and always present, though intensity fluctuates with emotional state, fatigue, and ambient light. No installed cybernetics visible. Hands show extensive manual wear and callus development consistent with unaugmented physical labor.
physical_description.posture_movement: Alert, economical movement with an instinctive awareness of vertical space and weight distribution. They move like someone comfortable in confined quarters and moving cargo â€” balance-first, every step calculated. Fidgets with hands when stationary (picking at scar, testing rope knots, checking equipment). When tired or lonely, they slouch slightly, making themselves smaller. Quick, infectious smile that doesn't reach their eyes until they trust someone.
physical_description.clothing_style: Pure Tier 4-5 transient: layered insulation wear in grays and deep blues, cargo pants with reinforced thigh and shin pockets, worn synthetic-leather boots with aggressive tread, salvaged thermal wrap worn as a coat or blanket depending on need. No corporate branding. Patches and repairs are functional, not aesthetic. Carries a battered chest harness with carabiners, rope, and cargo assessment tools. Everything smells faintly of lift-gas, ozone, and Lake Superior wind. Wears a single brass pressure gauge on a cord around their neck as a prayer object â€” the Ballast Keeper token.
